paper.title_en: Constraining Gamma-Ray Emission Beyond the TOV Limit: A Targeted Fermi-GBM Search for Counterparts to 39 LVK Gravitational-Wave Candidates in GWTC-5.0
paper.abstract_en: We present a systematic search for sub-threshold gamma-ray counterparts within a one-day time window of 161 gravitational-wave (GW) events from the GWTC-5.0 catalog, whose inferred source masses exceed the adopted Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff (TOV) limit, using the Gamma-ray Targeted Search (GTS) pipeline. The search identifies 39 candidate GW--gamma-ray pairs satisfying the adopted joint likelihood-ratio thresholds. None of these candidates exhibits a temporal offset compatible with the prompt-emission delay observed for GW170817 ($\sim 1.7$ s); the smallest temporal separation is 17 min 17.976 s, ruling out GW170817-like prompt temporal associations in our candidate sample. Several candidates nevertheless show substantial spatial consistency. In particular, the most spatially consistent pair has a joint localization overlap of 95.4%, despite a temporal separation of 13 h 19 min 8.85 s, illustrating that high spatial agreement can occur by chance in the absence of temporal consistency. Among the sub-threshold gamma-ray candidates, we further identify an anomalous event with an exceptionally large single-instrument significance of log LR = 5250.84. For comparison, the adopted $3σ$ threshold corresponds to log LR $\approx 9$. The extreme likelihood ratio of this candidate motivates further investigation of trigger sensitivity, onboard veto configurations, and the statistical interpretation of sub-threshold events. Overall, we find no physically viable multi-messenger associations between the GWTC-5.0 events and the searched gamma-ray candidates, and derive corresponding upper limits on prompt high-energy emission from GWTC-5.0 progenitors.
